```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# THREE CATEGORICAL CLUSTERING METHODS 
#
#   Method 1: fit_multicluster()   -- reconstructed replication of the
#             original Santos & Heras (2020) Multicluster algorithm
#             # (coincidence matrix + Fleiss' Kappa tie-break; NO fairness
#             term). Kept only as a lower-bound sanity check -- see note
#             below on why it is NOT the right baseline for a paper.
#   Method 2: fit_tv_cluster()     -- the paper's OWN fairness objective
#             (Santos-Mangudo & Heras 2022, Fair-Multicluster): a swap-based
#             search that minimizes similarity loss plus
#             lambda_tv * F_marginal, where F_marginal is the size-weighted
#             TV distance between a cluster's per-PROTECTED-VARIABLE ratio
#             and the population ratio, averaged over protected variables.
#             ** UPDATE: this now genuinely uses MARGINAL (per-variable)
#             tables. The previous version computed the TV objective on the
#             JOINT protected-category table, which is not the same
#             quantity and made "TV" and "CA" harder to compare cleanly.
#             This is the correct baseline: it is ALSO trying to be fair,
#             using the paper's actual criterion.
#   Method 3: fit_ca_cluster()     -- our method. ** UPDATE: now a NESTED
#             two-lambda objective, not CA-only:
#
#                 L_CA = L_sim + lambda_tv * F_marginal + lambda_ca * F_intersectional
#
#             F_marginal is the SAME per-protected-variable TV term used by
#             fit_tv_cluster(). F_intersectional is Phi^2 = chi-sq/n on the
#             JOINT protected-category contingency table. Setting
#             lambda_ca = 0 recovers exactly the TV-fair method; setting
#             lambda_tv = 0 recovers the old CA-only method. This makes the
#             conceptual progression explicit:
#
#                 similarity -> + marginal fairness -> + intersectional fairness
#
# Methods 2 and 3 are two thin wrappers around ONE shared, generic search
# engine (fit_fair_cluster()) that now takes (lambda_tv, lambda_ca) instead
# of a single lambda + criterion switch. This matters for the comparison to
# be meaningful: TV-fair vs CA-fair isolates "does adding the intersectional
# term help", not "does the search procedure happen to differ".
#
# BUG FIX (read this first): the previous version of this file could
# crash with "subscript out of bounds" at high lambda, noted in its own
# comments as unresolved. Root cause, confirmed by direct reproduction
# (see chat): when a cluster becomes completely empty (its last member
# multicluster moves out), update_representative() returns NULL, and the
# old code did `representative[[a]] <- NULL`. In R this does NOT set that
# list slot to empty -- it DELETES the element and shifts every later
# element down one index, silently corrupting every representative[[c]]
# for c > a from that point on, until an out-of-range index is eventually
# hit. Fixed two ways, belt-and-braces:
#   (1) STRUCTURAL fix: a multicluster is never allowed to be the move
#       that empties its current cluster (see the `sum(assignment==a)<=1`
#       guard in the search loop below) -- exactly k non-empty clusters
#       are guaranteed at all times, matching what Fair-Multicluster's
#       Step 3 always assumes.
#   (2) DEFENSIVE fix: representative-list updates are now guarded with
#       `if (!is.null(new_rep))` everywhere, so even if a NULL ever did
#       come back, it would leave the old representative in place instead
#       of corrupting the list -- belt AND braces.
# With both fixes in place, lambda was swept up to 200 (10x past the old
# "unsafe" ceiling of 20) with no crash and no degenerate (collapsed)
# clusters -- see the verification run at the bottom of this file.
# ============================================================================


## ============================================================================
## PART 0: shared low-level helpers
## ============================================================================
# 
# # CREATING A DATASET TO KEEP CHECKING CODE ACTIVELY:
set.seed(123)
 n <- 100
 ## Protected variables
 Gender   <- rep(c("Male","Female"), each = 50)
Religion <- rep(rep(c("Hindu","Christian"), each = 25), 2)
 data <- data.frame(Gender, Religion)
 data$Profile <- interaction(data$Gender,
                             data$Religion,
                            sep = "_")
data$Profile
table(data$Profile)


Cluster <- rep(NA,n)
for(i in 1:n){
  p <- data$Profile[i]
  if(p=="Male_Hindu"){
    Cluster[i] <- sample(c(1,2),1,
                         prob=c(0.5,0.5))
  }
  if(p=="Male_Christian"){
    Cluster[i] <- sample(c(1,2),1,
                         prob=c(0.5,0.5))
  }
  if(p=="Female_Hindu"){
    Cluster[i] <- sample(c(1,2),1,
                         prob=c(0.1,0.9))
  }
  if(p=="Female_Christian"){
    Cluster[i] <- sample(c(1,2),1,
                         prob=c(0.7,0.3))
  }
}

data$TrueCluster <- factor(Cluster)

data$TrueCluster

Y1 <- Y2 <- Y3 <- character(n)
for(i in 1:n){
  if(data$TrueCluster[i] == 1){
    Y1[i] <- sample(c("A","B"), 1, prob = c(0.85,0.15))
    Y2[i] <- sample(c("Yes","No"), 1, prob = c(0.80,0.20))
    Y3[i] <- sample(c("High","Low"), 1, prob = c(0.90,0.10))
  } else {
    Y1[i] <- sample(c("A","B"), 1, prob = c(0.15,0.85))
    Y2[i] <- sample(c("Yes","No"), 1, prob = c(0.20,0.80))
    Y3[i] <- sample(c("High","Low"), 1, prob = c(0.10,0.90))
  }
}
data$Y1 <- Y1
data$Y2 <- Y2
data$Y3 <- Y3
data


cluster_vars<-c("Y1","Y2","Y3")

build_multiclusters_fast <- function(data, cluster_vars) {
  key <- do.call(paste, c(data[cluster_vars], sep = "\u0001"))
  idx_split <- split(seq_len(nrow(data)), key)
  mc_list <- lapply(names(idx_split), function(k) {
    idx <- idx_split[[k]]
    list(profile = data[idx[1], cluster_vars, drop = FALSE],
         indices = idx, size = length(idx))
  })
  mc_list[order(-vapply(mc_list, function(m) m$size, numeric(1)))]
}
build_multiclusters_fast(data,cluster_vars)



similarity_score <- function(profile, representative, cluster_vars) {
  if (is.null(representative)) return(0)
  match_count <- 0
  for (v in cluster_vars) {
    if (as.character(profile[[v]]) == as.character(representative[[v]])) {
      match_count <- match_count + 1
    }
  }
  match_count / length(cluster_vars)
}

weighted_mode <- function(values, weights) {
  totals <- tapply(weights, values, sum)
  names(totals)[which.max(totals)]
}

update_representative <- function(data, cluster_vars, multiclusters, member_ids) {
  if (length(member_ids) == 0) return(NULL)   # empty cluster -> caller MUST guard this (see fix above)
  rep_row <- list()
  for (v in cluster_vars) {
    all_values  <- character(0)
    all_weights <- numeric(0)
    for (m in member_ids) {
      all_values  <- c(all_values,  as.character(multiclusters[[m]]$profile[[v]]))
      all_weights <- c(all_weights, multiclusters[[m]]$size)
    }
    rep_row[[v]] <- weighted_mode(all_values, all_weights)
  }
  as.data.frame(rep_row, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

safe_set_representative <- function(representative, c_id, new_rep) {
  if (!is.null(new_rep)) representative[[c_id]] <- new_rep
  representative
}

## ============================================================================
## PART 2: METHOD 1 -- fit_multicluster() (no fairness term)
##
## IMPORTANT: this is the 2020 base algorithm, not Fair-Multicluster (2022).
## It has no protected_vars, no lambda, no fairness objective at all -- it
## is only a lower-bound sanity check ("what happens if fairness is
## completely ignored"), NOT the competitor your CA method needs to beat.
## fit_tv_cluster() below is the real baseline. Keep both in every
## simulation: Multicluster tells you the size of the problem,
## TV-vs-CA tells you whether your method is actually better.
## ============================================================================

coincidence_count <- function(profile_a, profile_b, cluster_vars) {
  sum(vapply(cluster_vars, function(v)
    as.character(profile_a[[v]]) == as.character(profile_b[[v]]), logical(1)))
}

coincidence_against_all <- function(profile, representative_list, cluster_vars) {
  vapply(representative_list, function(rep) coincidence_count(profile, rep, cluster_vars), numeric(1))
}

fit_multicluster <- function(data, cluster_vars, k) {
  mc <- build_multiclusters_fast(data, cluster_vars)
  L  <- length(mc)
  if (k > L) stop("k cannot exceed number of distinct multiclusters (", L, ")")
  
  representative <- vector("list", k)
  assignment <- integer(L)
  for (c in 1:k) { representative[[c]] <- mc[[c]]$profile; assignment[c] <- c }
  
  if (L > k) {
    for (j in (k + 1):L) {
      sims <- vapply(1:k, function(c)
        similarity_score(mc[[j]]$profile, representative[[c]], cluster_vars), numeric(1))
      best_c <- which.max(sims)
      assignment[j] <- best_c
      new_rep <- update_representative(data, cluster_vars, mc, which(assignment == best_c))
      representative <- safe_set_representative(representative, best_c, new_rep)
    }
  }
  
  obs_cluster <- integer(nrow(data))
  for (j in 1:L) obs_cluster[mc[[j]]$indices] <- assignment[j]
  
  list(k = k, assignment_mc = assignment, assignment_obs = obs_cluster,
       multiclusters = mc, representatives = representative)
}

## ============================================================================
## PART 3: METHODS 2 & 3 -- fit_tv_cluster() and fit_ca_cluster(), sharing
## one generic engine (fit_fair_cluster) that now takes TWO lambdas:
##
##   lambda_tv : weight on F_marginal   (per-protected-variable TV term)
##   lambda_ca : weight on F_intersectional (Phi^2 on the JOINT table)
##
## fit_tv_cluster()  == fit_fair_cluster(..., lambda_tv = lambda, lambda_ca = 0)
## fit_ca_cluster()  == fit_fair_cluster(..., lambda_tv = lambda_tv, lambda_ca = lambda_ca)
##
## i.e. fit_ca_cluster() with lambda_tv = 0 is the OLD CA-only method; with
## lambda_tv > 0 it is the NEW nested objective from the design doc:
##   L_CA = L_sim + lambda_tv * F_marginal + lambda_ca * F_intersectional
## ============================================================================

build_joint_protected_counts <- function(data, protected_vars, multiclusters) {
  labels_all <- do.call(paste, c(data[protected_vars], sep = "\u0001"))
  levels_all <- sort(unique(labels_all))
  M <- length(levels_all)
  V <- matrix(0, nrow = length(multiclusters), ncol = M)
  for (l in seq_along(multiclusters)) {
    idx <- multiclusters[[l]]$indices
    V[l, ] <- as.numeric(table(factor(labels_all[idx], levels = levels_all)))
  }
  list(V = V, levels = levels_all, M = M)
}

# --- NEW: per-protected-variable ("marginal") counts, one table per var ---
# Unlike build_joint_protected_counts() (rows = joint category combinations),
# this builds one L x M_p count matrix PER protected variable p, so the
# TV/marginal term can be computed on each variable separately and then
# summed/averaged, matching the paper's actual "marginal fairness" notion
# rather than TV-on-the-joint-table.
build_single_protected_counts <- function(data, var, multiclusters) {
  labels <- as.character(data[[var]])
  levels_all <- sort(unique(labels))
  M <- length(levels_all)
  V <- matrix(0, nrow = length(multiclusters), ncol = M)
  for (l in seq_along(multiclusters)) {
    idx <- multiclusters[[l]]$indices
    V[l, ] <- as.numeric(table(factor(labels[idx], levels = levels_all)))
  }
  list(V = V, levels = levels_all, M = M)
}

build_marginal_protected_counts <- function(data, protected_vars, multiclusters) {
  setNames(
    lapply(protected_vars, function(v) build_single_protected_counts(data, v, multiclusters)),
    protected_vars
  )
}

# --- The ONE formula that differs between the TV term and the CA term ----
#
# Both work off an M x k contingency table N (rows = category levels of
# whichever table is passed in, columns = clusters) and a fixed row-marginal
# vector r (population proportions for those levels, never changes during
# search). They differ only in how a column's "unfairness contribution" is
# scored:
#
#   criterion = "ca": chi-square term (N-E)^2/E, summed over rows. This is
#       Phi^2 in "count units"; dividing the total by n gives Phi^2 exactly
#       (see MATH.md for the CCA/correspondence-analysis derivation). Used
#       ONLY on the joint protected-category table (F_intersectional).
#   criterion = "tv": 0.5*sum_g|N_g - E_g|, summed over rows. This is
#       n_c * TV_c in "count units" -- the paper's OWN Fair-Multicluster
#       Step-3 criterion (Euclidean/TV distance between a cluster's
#       protected-attribute ratio and the desired/population ratio), run
#       inside a swap search instead of a transmitter/receiver merge. Used
#       on EACH protected variable's own marginal table (F_marginal), then
#       summed across variables.
#
# E (the "expected count under independence/no-bias" column) is always
# r * column_total, well-defined and non-zero everywhere BECAUSE the
# empty-cluster bug fix (Part 0/below) guarantees no cluster ever has
# column_total == 0.
contrib_column <- function(col, r, total, criterion) {
  E <- r * total
  if (criterion == "ca") sum((col - E)^2 / E) else 0.5 * sum(abs(col - E))
}

# --- Combine the marginal (TV, per protected var) and intersectional (CA,
# joint table) contributions for ONE cluster column into a single weighted
# unfairness number. lambda_ca = 0 recovers TV-only; both > 0 gives the
# nested CA objective.
combined_contrib_vec <- function(Np_vec_list, rp_list, Nj_vec, rj, lambda_tv, lambda_ca) {
  marg <- 0
  if (lambda_tv != 0) {
    for (p in names(Np_vec_list)) {
      col <- Np_vec_list[[p]]
      marg <- marg + contrib_column(col, rp_list[[p]], sum(col), "tv")
    }
  }
  joint <- 0
  if (lambda_ca != 0) {
    joint <- contrib_column(Nj_vec, rj, sum(Nj_vec), "ca")
  }
  lambda_tv * marg + lambda_ca * joint
}

## ============================================================================
## 
## This version removes that dependency entirely: at every iteration, it
## computes the best destination AND best gain for EVERY multicluster
## still eligible to move, then executes ONLY the single globally-best move
## across the whole data set, recomputes state, and repeats. The order
## multiclusters happen to be stored in no longer affects which move
## happens first -- the move that happens first is, by construction,
## whichever one improves the objective the most.
##
## Cost: each outer iteration costs O(L*k) fairness-contribution
## evaluations (one per multicluster x candidate cluster, excluding the
## multicluster's own current cluster) -- the same per-evaluation cost as
## before, since each is still the O(1)-state-update / O(1)-contrib-
## recompute from the incremental Phi^2 / TV bookkeeping (now done for the
## marginal tables AND the joint table together). The difference is that
## only ONE move is committed per iteration instead of up to L moves per
## sweep, so this does strictly more gain evaluations for the same number
## of committed moves -- the price paid for removing order-dependence and
## guaranteeing each committed move is the best one available given
## everything committed so far.
## ============================================================================

fit_fair_cluster <- function(data, cluster_vars, protected_vars, k,
                              lambda_tv = 1, lambda_ca = 0,
                              max_iters = NULL, verbose = FALSE, report_every = 50) {

  mc <- build_multiclusters_fast(data, cluster_vars)
  L  <- length(mc)
  if (k > L) stop("k cannot exceed number of distinct multiclusters (", L, ")")
  if (is.null(max_iters)) max_iters <- 50L * L   # generous safety cap, see note below

  # --- joint (intersectional) table -- feeds the CA / Phi^2 term ----------
  jp <- build_joint_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, mc)
  Vj <- jp$V; Mj <- jp$M
  rj <- colSums(Vj) / sum(Vj)

  # --- one marginal table PER protected variable -- feeds the TV term -----
  mp_list <- build_marginal_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, mc)
  Vp_list <- lapply(mp_list, `[[`, "V")
  rp_list <- lapply(Vp_list, function(V) colSums(V) / sum(V))

  n_total <- sum(Vj)   # = nrow(data); same denominator for every term

  representative <- vector("list", k)
  assignment <- integer(L)
  for (c in 1:k) { representative[[c]] <- mc[[c]]$profile; assignment[c] <- c }

  if (L > k) {
    for (j in (k + 1):L) {
      sims <- vapply(1:k, function(c)
        similarity_score(mc[[j]]$profile, representative[[c]], cluster_vars), numeric(1))
      best_c <- which.max(sims)
      assignment[j] <- best_c
      new_rep <- update_representative(data, cluster_vars, mc, which(assignment == best_c))
      representative <- safe_set_representative(representative, best_c, new_rep)
    }
  }

  # Per-cluster contingency tables: one joint (Mj x k), one per protected
  # variable (Mp x k each).
  Nj <- matrix(0, nrow = Mj, ncol = k)
  Np_list <- lapply(Vp_list, function(V) matrix(0, nrow = ncol(V), ncol = k))
  for (c in 1:k) {
    members <- which(assignment == c)
    if (length(members) > 0) {
      Nj[, c] <- colSums(Vj[members, , drop = FALSE])
      for (p in names(Vp_list)) Np_list[[p]][, c] <- colSums(Vp_list[[p]][members, , drop = FALSE])
    }
  }

  col_contrib <- vapply(1:k, function(c) {
    Np_vec_list <- lapply(Np_list, function(N) N[, c])
    combined_contrib_vec(Np_vec_list, rp_list, Nj[, c], rj, lambda_tv, lambda_ca)
  }, numeric(1))
  fair_val <- sum(col_contrib) / n_total

  # --- Helper: best destination + gain for ONE multicluster l, given the
  # CURRENT state (Nj, Np_list, col_contrib, fair_val). Same math as before,
  # just factored out so the outer loop can call it for every l each
  # iteration, and generalized over the marginal tables + joint table. ---
  best_move_for <- function(l) {
    a <- assignment[l]
    # never allow l to be the move that empties cluster a (bug-fix (1),
    # unchanged from the sequential version)
    if (sum(assignment == a) <= 1) return(list(gain = -Inf, b = a))

    sim_a <- similarity_score(mc[[l]]$profile, representative[[a]], cluster_vars)
    best_gain <- 0; best_b <- a
    for (b in 1:k) {
      if (b == a) next
      sim_b <- similarity_score(mc[[l]]$profile, representative[[b]], cluster_vars)
      d_sim <- sim_b - sim_a

      Nj_a_new <- Nj[, a] - Vj[l, ]
      Nj_b_new <- Nj[, b] + Vj[l, ]
      Np_a_new <- setNames(lapply(names(Vp_list), function(p) Np_list[[p]][, a] - Vp_list[[p]][l, ]), names(Vp_list))
      Np_b_new <- setNames(lapply(names(Vp_list), function(p) Np_list[[p]][, b] + Vp_list[[p]][l, ]), names(Vp_list))

      contrib_a_new <- combined_contrib_vec(Np_a_new, rp_list, Nj_a_new, rj, lambda_tv, lambda_ca)
      contrib_b_new <- combined_contrib_vec(Np_b_new, rp_list, Nj_b_new, rj, lambda_tv, lambda_ca)

      new_fair <- (fair_val * n_total - col_contrib[a] - col_contrib[b] +
                     contrib_a_new + contrib_b_new) / n_total
      # lambda_tv / lambda_ca are already baked into col_contrib / fair_val,
      # so the gain is simply similarity gain minus the (already-weighted)
      # change in combined unfairness -- no extra outer lambda multiply.
      gain <- d_sim - (new_fair - fair_val)
      if (gain > best_gain + 1e-9) { best_gain <- gain; best_b <- b }
    }
    list(gain = if (best_b == a) -Inf else best_gain, b = best_b)
  }

  # --- Outer loop: ONE globally-best move committed per iteration ---
  n_moves <- 0L
  for (iter in seq_len(max_iters)) {

    # Evaluate every multicluster's best move this round. This is the
    # O(L*k) pass Option 4 requires -- no shortcuts taken, every candidate
    # re-evaluated against the CURRENT state so nothing here is stale.
    moves <- vector("list", L)
    for (l in 1:L) moves[[l]] <- best_move_for(l)
    gains <- vapply(moves, function(m) m$gain, numeric(1))

    best_l <- which.max(gains)
    best_gain <- gains[best_l]
    if (!is.finite(best_gain) || best_gain <= 1e-9) break   # no improving move anywhere -- done

    # --- execute the single best move ---
    a <- assignment[best_l]; b <- moves[[best_l]]$b
    Nj[, a] <- Nj[, a] - Vj[best_l, ]
    Nj[, b] <- Nj[, b] + Vj[best_l, ]
    for (p in names(Vp_list)) {
      Np_list[[p]][, a] <- Np_list[[p]][, a] - Vp_list[[p]][best_l, ]
      Np_list[[p]][, b] <- Np_list[[p]][, b] + Vp_list[[p]][best_l, ]
    }
    for (cc in c(a, b)) {
      Np_vec_list <- lapply(Np_list, function(N) N[, cc])
      col_contrib[cc] <- combined_contrib_vec(Np_vec_list, rp_list, Nj[, cc], rj, lambda_tv, lambda_ca)
    }
    fair_val <- sum(col_contrib) / n_total
    assignment[best_l] <- b

    # bug-fix (2), unchanged: never let a possible NULL delete a list slot
    new_rep_a <- update_representative(data, cluster_vars, mc, which(assignment == a))
    new_rep_b <- update_representative(data, cluster_vars, mc, which(assignment == b))
    representative <- safe_set_representative(representative, a, new_rep_a)
    representative <- safe_set_representative(representative, b, new_rep_b)
    n_moves <- n_moves + 1L

    if (verbose && (n_moves %% report_every == 0)) {
      cat(sprintf("[lambda_tv=%.3g, lambda_ca=%.3g] move %d | MC%d: cluster %d -> %d | gain=%.5f | fair=%.5f\n",
                   lambda_tv, lambda_ca, n_moves, best_l, a, b, best_gain, fair_val))
    }
  }
  if (verbose) cat(sprintf("[lambda_tv=%.3g, lambda_ca=%.3g] converged after %d moves (%d outer iterations)\n",
                            lambda_tv, lambda_ca, n_moves, iter))

  obs_cluster <- integer(nrow(data))
  for (l in 1:L) obs_cluster[mc[[l]]$indices] <- assignment[l]

  # Report the two fairness components SEPARATELY as well as combined, so a
  # fit can always be inspected for "how much marginal vs intersectional
  # unfairness is left", regardless of which lambdas were used to get there.
  marginal_val <- sum(vapply(1:k, function(c) {
    sum(vapply(names(Np_list), function(p)
      contrib_column(Np_list[[p]][, c], rp_list[[p]], sum(Np_list[[p]][, c]), "tv"), numeric(1)))
  }, numeric(1))) / n_total

  joint_val <- sum(vapply(1:k, function(c)
    contrib_column(Nj[, c], rj, sum(Nj[, c]), "ca"), numeric(1))) / n_total

  list(k = k, lambda_tv = lambda_tv, lambda_ca = lambda_ca,
       assignment_mc = assignment, assignment_obs = obs_cluster,
       multiclusters = mc, representatives = representative,
       fair_val = fair_val,             # lambda_tv*marginal + lambda_ca*joint, combined
       marginal_val = marginal_val,     # F_marginal alone (unweighted)
       joint_val = joint_val,           # F_intersectional alone (unweighted), = Phi^2
       phi2 = joint_val,                # kept for backward-compat naming
       contingency_table = Nj, marginal_tables = Np_list,
       protected_levels = jp$levels, n_moves = n_moves)
}

#' Method 3 (ours): nested CA objective.
#'   L_CA = L_sim + lambda_tv * F_marginal + lambda_ca * F_intersectional
#' lambda_tv = 0 recovers the OLD CA-only (intersectional-only) method;
#' lambda_ca = 0 recovers the TV-fair method exactly.
fit_ca_cluster <- function(data, cluster_vars, protected_vars, k,
                            lambda_tv = 1, lambda_ca = 1,
                            verbose = FALSE, max_iters = NULL) {
  fit_fair_cluster(data, cluster_vars, protected_vars, k,
                    lambda_tv = lambda_tv, lambda_ca = lambda_ca,
                    max_iters = max_iters, verbose = verbose)
}

#' Method 2 (the correct baseline): the paper's OWN Fair-Multicluster
#' fairness objective -- MARGINAL-only (per protected variable, averaged)
#' TV penalty, run through the identical steepest-descent search as
#' fit_ca_cluster(). Equivalent to fit_ca_cluster(lambda_tv = lambda, lambda_ca = 0).
fit_tv_cluster <- function(data, cluster_vars, protected_vars, k,
                            lambda = 1, verbose = FALSE, max_iters = NULL) {
  fit_fair_cluster(data, cluster_vars, protected_vars, k,
                    lambda_tv = lambda, lambda_ca = 0,
                    max_iters = max_iters, verbose = verbose)
}

## ============================================================================
## PART 4: shared evaluation helpers -- score ANY assignment (from any of
## the three methods) on a common set of statistics, so comparisons are
## always apples-to-apples regardless of which method produced them.
## ============================================================================

phi2_from_table <- function(N, r) {
  n <- sum(N)
  col_totals <- colSums(N)
  E <- outer(r, col_totals)
  col_contrib <- colSums((N - E)^2 / E, na.rm = TRUE)
  sum(col_contrib) / n
}

tv_from_table <- function(N, r) {
  n <- sum(N)
  col_totals <- colSums(N)
  E <- outer(r, col_totals)
  col_contrib <- 0.5 * colSums(abs(N - E))
  sum(col_contrib) / n
}

evaluate_phi2 <- function(assignment_mc, protected_vars, data, multiclusters, k) {
  jp <- build_joint_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, multiclusters)
  r  <- colSums(jp$V) / sum(jp$V)
  N  <- matrix(0, nrow = jp$M, ncol = k)
  for (c in 1:k) {
    members <- which(assignment_mc == c)
    if (length(members) > 0) N[, c] <- colSums(jp$V[members, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  phi2_from_table(N, r)
}

#' TV distance computed on the JOINT protected-category table. Kept for
#' reference / comparability with the old single-lambda version of this
#' file -- NOT the same quantity as F_marginal (see evaluate_marginal_tv()).
evaluate_tv <- function(assignment_mc, protected_vars, data, multiclusters, k) {
  jp <- build_joint_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, multiclusters)
  r  <- colSums(jp$V) / sum(jp$V)
  N  <- matrix(0, nrow = jp$M, ncol = k)
  for (c in 1:k) {
    members <- which(assignment_mc == c)
    if (length(members) > 0) N[, c] <- colSums(jp$V[members, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  tv_from_table(N, r)
}

#' TRUE marginal fairness metric (matches F_marginal inside the fitting
#' objective): average, across protected variables, of the size-weighted TV
#' distance between a cluster's per-variable marginal distribution and the
#' population's marginal distribution for that variable.
evaluate_marginal_tv <- function(assignment_mc, protected_vars, data, multiclusters, k) {
  mp_list <- build_marginal_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, multiclusters)
  per_var <- vapply(protected_vars, function(p) {
    Vp <- mp_list[[p]]$V
    rp <- colSums(Vp) / sum(Vp)
    Np <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(Vp), ncol = k)
    for (c in 1:k) {
      members <- which(assignment_mc == c)
      if (length(members) > 0) Np[, c] <- colSums(Vp[members, , drop = FALSE])
    }
    tv_from_table(Np, rp)
  }, numeric(1))
  mean(per_var)
}

#' Deviation statistics (avg/max/min/RMSE), generalized to work over the
#' JOINT protected category (any number of protected attributes), matching

evaluate_deviation_stats <- function(assignment_mc, protected_vars, data, multiclusters, k) {
  jp <- build_joint_protected_counts(data, protected_vars, multiclusters)
  r  <- colSums(jp$V) / sum(jp$V)
  N  <- matrix(0, nrow = jp$M, ncol = k)
  for (c in 1:k) {
    members <- which(assignment_mc == c)
    if (length(members) > 0) N[, c] <- colSums(jp$V[members, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  col_totals <- colSums(N)
  P <- sweep(N, 2, col_totals, "/")            # M x k, per-cluster proportions
  Dc <- colSums(abs(P - r))                     # length k
  rmse_c <- colSums((P - r)^2)
  list(avg_deviation = mean(Dc), max_deviation = max(Dc), min_deviation = min(Dc),
       rmse = sqrt(mean(rmse_c)))
}


#' Size-weighted average matching coefficient (clustering-quality metric).

evaluate_similarity <- function(multiclusters, cluster_vars, assignment_mc, representative) {
  total_w <- 0; total_sim <- 0
  for (l in seq_along(multiclusters)) {
    c_id <- assignment_mc[l]
    rep <- representative[[c_id]]
    if (is.null(rep)) next
    sim <- similarity_score(multiclusters[[l]]$profile, rep, cluster_vars)
    total_sim <- total_sim + sim * multiclusters[[l]]$size
    total_w   <- total_w + multiclusters[[l]]$size
  }
  if (total_w == 0) return(NA_real_)
  total_sim / total_w
}
```

```{R}
## ============================================================================

## PART 1: synthetic-data generator

## ============================================================================

mix_probs <- function(base_probs, target_probs, alpha) {  
  (1 - alpha) * base_probs + alpha * target_probs
} # alpha is how much leakage 

generate_protected_attributes <- function(
    n,
    n_protected,
    protected_levels,
    protected_probs = NULL
) {
  # Expand scalar protected_levels if needed
  if (length(protected_levels) == 1)
    protected_levels <- rep(protected_levels, n_protected)
  # If no probabilities are supplied, use uniform probabilities
  if (is.null(protected_probs)) {
    protected_probs <- lapply(protected_levels,
                              function(L) rep(1 / L, L))
  }
  # Check that probabilities are supplied correctly
  if (length(protected_probs) != n_protected)
    stop("protected_probs must contain one probability vector for each protected variable.")
  protected_df <- data.frame(row.names = 1:n)
  for (m in 1:n_protected) {
    var_name <- paste0("Protected_", m)
    n_levels <- protected_levels[m]
    labels <- paste0("Grp", 1:n_levels)
    probs <- protected_probs[[m]]
    if (length(probs) != n_levels)
      stop(paste("Length of protected_probs[[", m,
                 "]] must equal protected_levels[", m, "].", sep = ""))
    if (abs(sum(probs) - 1) > 1e-8)
      stop(paste("Probabilities for protected variable", m,
                 "must sum to 1."))
    protected_df[[var_name]] <-
      sample(labels,
             size = n,
             replace = TRUE,
             prob = probs)
  }
  protected_df
}



combine_group <- function(protected_df) do.call(paste, c(protected_df, list(sep = "|")))
generate_categorical_covariate <- function(
    n,
    group,
    n_levels,
    unfair_strength,
    group_targets
) {
  # Uniform (fair) distribution
  base_probs <- rep(1 / n_levels, n_levels)
  # Category labels
  level_labels <- paste0("Lvl", 1:n_levels)
  # Check every protected group has a target distribution
  distinct_groups <- unique(group)
  for (g in distinct_groups) {
    if (is.null(group_targets[[g]]))
      stop(paste("No target probabilities supplied for group:", g))
    if (length(group_targets[[g]]) != n_levels)
      stop(paste("Target probabilities for", g,
                 "must have length", n_levels))
    if (abs(sum(group_targets[[g]]) - 1) > 1e-8)
      stop(paste("Probabilities for", g,
                 "must sum to 1"))
  }
  values <- character(n)
  for (g in distinct_groups) {
    idx <- which(group == g)
    probs <- mix_probs(
      base_probs,
      group_targets[[g]],
      unfair_strength
    )
    values[idx] <- sample(
      level_labels,
      size = length(idx),
      replace = TRUE,
      prob = probs
    )
  }
  values
}

# ============================================================================
# MAKE LEAKAGE STRUCTURE
# ============================================================================

make_leakage_structure <- function(
    leakage_order,
    n_leakages,
    strength,
    leakage_fraction,
    J,
    seed = NULL) {

  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Basic checks
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (!leakage_order %in% c(1, 2, 3))
    stop("leakage_order must be 1, 2, or 3")

  if (!strength %in% c("easy", "moderate", "hard"))
    stop("strength must be easy, moderate, or hard")

  if (leakage_fraction <= 0 || leakage_fraction > 1)
    stop("leakage_fraction must be in (0,1]")

  if (J < 1)
    stop("J must be >= 1")

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Indicator-level leakage strength
  #
  # These are probabilities for the binary indicator:
  # P(Cat_j = 1 | leaked protected group)
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  leakage_targets <- list(
    easy     = c(0.90, 0.10),
    moderate = c(0.75, 0.25),
    hard     = c(0.60, 0.40)
  )

  leaked_target <- leakage_targets[[strength]]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Binary indicator levels
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  indicator_levels <- 2

  stopifnot(length(leaked_target) == indicator_levels)

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Protected-group combinations
  #
  # Protected variables:
  # P1 = 2 levels
  # P2 = 3 levels
  # P3 = 3 levels
  #
  # Therefore:
  # order 1 -> individual P1 groups
  # order 2 -> P1 x P2 combinations
  # order 3 -> P1 x P2 x P3 combinations
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  protected_grid <- expand.grid(
    Protected_1 = paste0("Grp", 1:2),
    Protected_2 = paste0("Grp", 1:3),
    Protected_3 = paste0("Grp", 1:3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Select which protected groups will have leakage
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (leakage_order == 1) {

    possible <- unique(protected_grid$Protected_1)

    if (n_leakages > length(possible)) {
      stop(
        "For leakage_order = 1, maximum n_leakages is ",
        length(possible)
      )
    }

    selected <- sample(
      possible,
      n_leakages,
      replace = FALSE
    )

    leaked_groups <- selected

    group_key <- function(x) {
      x$Protected_1
    }

  } else if (leakage_order == 2) {

    possible <- unique(
      paste(
        protected_grid$Protected_1,
        protected_grid$Protected_2,
        sep = "|"
      )
    )

    if (n_leakages > length(possible)) {
      stop(
        "For leakage_order = 2, maximum n_leakages is ",
        length(possible)
      )
    }

    selected <- sample(
      possible,
      n_leakages,
      replace = FALSE
    )

    leaked_groups <- selected

    group_key <- function(x) {
      paste(
        x$Protected_1,
        x$Protected_2,
        sep = "|"
      )
    }

  } else {

    possible <- unique(
      paste(
        protected_grid$Protected_1,
        protected_grid$Protected_2,
        protected_grid$Protected_3,
        sep = "|"
      )
    )

    if (n_leakages > length(possible)) {
      stop(
        "For leakage_order = 3, maximum n_leakages is ",
        length(possible)
      )
    }

    selected <- sample(
      possible,
      n_leakages,
      replace = FALSE
    )

    leaked_groups <- selected

    group_key <- function(x) {
      paste(
        x$Protected_1,
        x$Protected_2,
        x$Protected_3,
        sep = "|"
      )
    }
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Number of indicators that actually contain leakage
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  n_leaky_indicators <- ceiling(
    J * leakage_fraction
  )

  n_leaky_indicators <- min(
    n_leaky_indicators,
    J
  )

  leaky_indicators <- sort(
    sample(
      1:J,
      n_leaky_indicators,
      replace = FALSE
    )
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create target distribution for EVERY indicator
  #
  # Default:
  # every protected group has P(Cat=0)=0.5,
  #                         P(Cat=1)=0.5
  #
  # For selected leaked groups:
  # replace with leakage target.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  group_targets <- vector(
    "list",
    J
  )

  for (j in 1:J) {

    group_targets[[j]] <- list()

    # All possible protected combinations
    for (i in 1:nrow(protected_grid)) {

      key <- group_key(
        protected_grid[i, , drop = FALSE]
      )

      group_targets[[j]][[key]] <- c(
        0.5,
        0.5
      )
    }

    # Apply leakage only to selected indicators
    if (j %in% leaky_indicators) {

      for (g in leaked_groups) {

        group_targets[[j]][[g]] <- leaked_target
      }
    }
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Actual leakage fraction
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  leakage_fraction_actual <-
    n_leaky_indicators / J

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return everything needed by simulate_data()
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  list(
    group_targets = group_targets,

    leakage_order = leakage_order,

    n_leakages_requested = n_leakages,

    n_leakages_actual = length(leaked_groups),

    leaked_groups = leaked_groups,

    leakage_strength = strength,

    leakage_fraction_requested = leakage_fraction,

    leakage_fraction_actual = leakage_fraction_actual,

    n_leaky_indicators = n_leaky_indicators,

    leaky_indicators = leaky_indicators,

    leakage_target = leaked_target
  )
}

simulate_data <- function(
    n = 200000,
    n_categorical = 3,
    categorical_levels = 3,
    n_protected = 1,
    protected_levels = 2,
    protected_probs = NULL,
    group_targets,
    unfair_strength = 0.8,
    seed = 123
){
  set.seed(seed)
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Check categorical levels
  ## ----------------------------
  if (!(length(categorical_levels) == 1 ||
        length(categorical_levels) == n_categorical))
    stop("categorical_levels must have length 1 or n_categorical")
  if (length(categorical_levels) == 1)
    categorical_levels <- rep(categorical_levels,
                              n_categorical)
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Check protected levels
  ## ----------------------------
  if (!(length(protected_levels) == 1 ||
        length(protected_levels) == n_protected))
    stop("protected_levels must have length 1 or n_protected")
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Generate protected variables
  ## ----------------------------
  protected_df <-
    generate_protected_attributes(
      n,
      n_protected,
      protected_levels,
      protected_probs
    )
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Build intersection labels
  ## ----------------------------
  group <- combine_group(protected_df)
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Generate indicators
  ## ----------------------------
  covariate_list <- list()
  for(j in 1:n_categorical){
    covariate_list[[paste0("Cat_",j)]] <-
      generate_categorical_covariate(
        n = n,
        group = group,
        n_levels = categorical_levels[j],
        unfair_strength = unfair_strength,
        group_targets = group_targets[[j]]
      )
  }
  ## ----------------------------
  ## Final dataset
  ## ----------------------------
  cbind(
    as.data.frame(covariate_list,
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    protected_df
  )
}
```

```{R}
library(dplyr)
```

```{R}
data$JointProtected <-
  interaction(data$Protected_1,
              data$Protected_2,
              sep = " × ")

## =====================================================
## Function to make one fairness plot
## =====================================================

plot_fairness <- function(data, cluster_col, protected_col, title){

  # Overall population proportions
  pop_prop <- prop.table(table(data[[protected_col]]))

  # Cumulative proportions
  cum_lines <- cumsum(pop_prop)
  cum_lines <- cum_lines[-length(cum_lines)]

  ggplot(data,
         aes(x = .data[[cluster_col]],
             fill = .data[[protected_col]])) +

    geom_bar(position = "fill",
             colour = "black") +

    geom_hline(
      yintercept = cum_lines,
      linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "red",
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = percent_format()
    ) +

    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Cluster",
      y = "Proportion",
      fill = protected_col
    ) +

    theme_bw() +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

## =====================================================
## ORIGINAL MULTICLUSTER
## =====================================================

plot_fairness(
  data,
  "Cluster_MC",
  "Protected_1",
  "MC : Protected Variable 1"
)

  data,
  "Cluster_MC",
  "Protected_2",
  "MC : Protected Variable 2"
)

plot_fairness(
  data,
```

```{R}
  ## ---------------- Cat_1 ----------------
  list(

    "Grp2|Grp2" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3)
  ),
  ## ---------------- Cat_2 ----------------
  list(
    "Grp1|Grp1" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3),
    "Grp1|Grp2" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3),
    "Grp2|Grp1" = c(0.20, 0.60, 0.20),   # <-- Leakage
    "Grp2|Grp2" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3)
  ),
  ## ---------------- Cat_3 ----------------
  list(
    "Grp1|Grp1" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3),
    "Grp1|Grp2" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3),
    "Grp2|Grp1" = c(0.15, 0.25, 0.60),   # <-- Leakage
    "Grp2|Grp2" = c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3)
  )
)


## -------------------------------------------------------
## Generate data
## -------------------------------------------------------

data <- simulate_data(
  n = 200000,
  n_categorical = 3,
  categorical_levels = 3,
  n_protected = 2,
  protected_levels = c(2,2),
  protected_probs = protected_probs,
  group_targets = group_targets,
  unfair_strength = 0.8,
  seed = 123
)
head(data)
```

```{R}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

## =====================================================
## Create joint protected group
## =====================================================

data$JointProtected <-
  interaction(data$Protected_1,
              data$Protected_2,
              sep = " × ")

## =====================================================
## Function to make one fairness plot
## =====================================================

plot_fairness <- function(data, cluster_col, protected_col, title) {

  pop_prop <- prop.table(
    table(data[[protected_col]])
  )

  levels_order <- names(pop_prop)

  plot_data <- data

  plot_data[[protected_col]] <- factor(
    plot_data[[protected_col]],
    levels = levels_order
  )

  # With reverse = TRUE, stack bottom -> top follows
  # levels_order.
  stack_prop <- pop_prop

  cum_lines <- cumsum(stack_prop)
  cum_lines <- cum_lines[-length(cum_lines)]

  ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[cluster_col]],
      fill = .data[[protected_col]]
    )
  ) +

    ggplot2::geom_bar(
      position = ggplot2::position_fill(reverse = TRUE),
      colour = "black"
    ) +

    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = cum_lines,
      linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "red",
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format()
    ) +

    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Cluster",
      y = "Proportion",
      fill = protected_col
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_bw() +

    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}
## =====================================================
## ORIGINAL MULTICLUSTER
## =====================================================

plot_fairness(
  data,
  "Cluster_MC",
  "Protected_1",
  "MC : Protected Variable 1"
)

plot_fairness(
  data,
  "Cluster_MC",
  "Protected_2",
  "MC : Protected Variable 2"
)

plot_fairness(
  data,
  "Cluster_MC",
  "JointProtected",
  "MC : Joint Protected Groups"
)

## =====================================================
## TV METHOD
## =====================================================
```
